Understand.name: understand
Understand.description: Use when clarifying a request, resuming work, or identifying intent, constraints and observable success conditions.
steps: Read available request context and saved decisions before asking for information.
Establish the intended outcome, constraints and observable success conditions.
Ask about material ambiguity rather than guessing; scale clarification to the request.
Hand off the agreed outcome, constraints and success conditions without authorizing unrequested work.

Explore.name: explore
Explore.description: Use when investigating evidence, existing code and options before choosing an implementation approach.
steps: Inspect relevant sources, tests and callers; distinguish observed facts from assumptions.
Identify external dependencies and reuse existing boundary contracts and mocks before writing tests.
Compare relevant options, challenge weak assumptions and choose the simplest complete approach.
Resolve consequential scope and naming decisions with the user before acting.
Hand off evidence, the approach and required approvals; separate investigation does not transfer task ownership.

Make.name: make
Make.description: Use when producing an agreed change or artifact, including production coding, documentation or design.
steps: Produce the agreed artifact while preserving unrelated work and intended behavior.
For production behavior changes, load and follow [the TDD skill](../tdd/SKILL.md) before changing production code.
For documentation or design work, do not claim TDD execution.
Keep generation and business logic in functions where practical; keep UI components focused on presentation.
Hand off the change, verification evidence, blockers and limitations. Do not initiate commits.

Evaluate.name: evaluate
Evaluate.description: Use when assessing a result against success conditions, reviewing compliance or deciding the next step.
steps: Compare the result directly with agreed success conditions; tests and coverage are not substitutes for the requested outcome.
Use relevant runtime and UI evidence when necessary, including interactions and viewport sizes.
Review practice compliance separately from passing tests, coverage and builds.
For opted-in tracking, retain observed metrics and unknowns without inventing effort or user benefits.
Report failures and unavailable checks explicitly; decide whether to finish, revise or continue.
Being ready does not authorize a commit; the guide handles commits only on explicit request.
